graphHonesty.maxSafeConcurrencyRationale: Wave missions are dependency-free within their wave, but concurrency is bounded by three real constraints: (1) shared-repo surfaces — registry.json (M-R-04 single-writer), kernel/ sources (Kernel team serializes its own missions), canonical environment (M-R-100/85/101 exclusive access); (2) the verify pipeline is a shared resource with no correctness risk but real contention above ~10 parallel runs; (3) ADR-gated missions (M-R-50, M-R-83, M-R-111, M-R-121) cannot start before their rulings land. 10 concurrent missions is the honest ceiling; wave membership expresses readiness order, not simultaneous launch count.
forcedParallelismWarnings: The 50-mission count is derived, not forced: it is the set of missions dependency analysis actually proves; no filler missions were added to reach it and none of the STREAM J inflation candidates (twin runtime, simulation engines, SDK/marketplace, agent society, ontology compiler, globalization/enterprise/scheduling, ambient bridge, reality graph, CP-01..12 as full mechanisms, AI compute infrastructure) appear as missions.
Kernel missions M-R-10/11 are both wave-1 but share kernel/ sources: they are safe to run in parallel with other teams, NOT with each other — within-team one-writer rule applies.

M-R-04 (registry reconciliation) is wave-1 and parallelizable as repo work but is marked parallelizable:false because it rewrites registry.json while other missions concurrently edit phase contracts it validates — it must own the registry surface exclusively during its run.
